diagnostic_evidence.quote: then the column space of $W^{\frac{1}{2}} B^T$ deviates from all the coordinate $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathds{R}^n$ by at least $\arccos(1 / \sqrt{n})$
Our computer experiments described in the next section allow us to suggest that in reality the equality holds, and it is achieved on a finite number of subspaces.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract asserts a description of the class of all subspaces with deviation at least arccos(1/sqrt(n)). The only formal result (the Theorem) shows that the weighted star spaces of 2-sp-graphs belong to this class; the converse (every such subspace arises this way) is supported only by the numerical coincidence with the OEIS count, not by a proof.

failure_location.quote: we describe the class of subspaces deviating from all the coordinate ones by at least $\arccos(1 / \sqrt{n})$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase the abstract/introduction to state that a family of subspaces attaining deviation at least arccos(1/sqrt(n)) is constructed, with the completeness of the family being conjectural.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope (a characterization) exceeds what is established (a sufficient construction); the theorem and corollary themselves are unaffected.
issues.title: Abstract claims to describe the class of all extremal subspaces; only one inclusion is proved
issues.why_classification: Only the prose scope needs adjusting; every formal result and its proof survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $G$ be a 2-sp-graph with a pair of vertices treated as terminals, and let
According to Lemma 9 from \cite{Eppstein1992}, if $(l, r)$ is an edge in a 2-sp-graph, $l$ and $r$ can be treated as the terminals.
Let us consider two pairs of terminals in a 2-sp-graph and the corresponding decomposition trees $t$ and $\tilde{t}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition of G-induced weights and Proposition prw quantify over an arbitrary pair of vertices treated as terminals, but a 2-sp-graph need not be a 2-terminal series-parallel graph with respect to every vertex pair. Example: K4 minus an edge (a 2-sp-graph) with the two nonadjacent vertices as terminals has neither a parallel decomposition (removing the pair leaves a connected edge) nor a serial one (the graph is 2-connected), so no decomposition tree and no weights exist; the proposition's proof presupposes decomposition trees $t$ and $\tilde t$ for both pairs.

failure_location.quote: Graph-induced edge weights are invariant to the choice of terminals up to a common factor.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the definition and Proposition prw to terminal pairs for which G is a 2-terminal series-parallel graph (e.g., endpoints of an edge), which is all the theorem uses.
issues.overall_effect: The definition and proposition are ill-posed for inadmissible terminal pairs; the theorem, which only uses endpoints of an edge (justified by the cited Eppstein lemma), is not affected.
issues.title: G-induced weights and Proposition on terminal-invariance are stated for arbitrary terminal pairs, some of which admit no series-parallel decomposition
issues.why_classification: A local restriction of the hypothesis suffices; the proof and all downstream uses survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We leave it as an exercise for the reader to prove the following property.
Our next step is to show that $Y_{\tau} y_{\tau} = \frac{1}{n} y_{\tau}$, where $y_\tau$ is the restriction of the vector of $(G,\tau)$-induced coefficients to the set of $\tau$'s edges.
Let us denote $e_0$'s vertices by $l$ and $r$ and treat them as the terminals. We will also assume without loss of generality that all $G$'s edges are directed from $l$ to~$r$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the Theorem verifies the e_0-th component of Y_τ y_τ = (1/n) y_τ using the vector y_τ built with e_0's endpoints as terminals and with edges oriented relative to those terminals; e_0 ranges over all edges of τ. To conclude that a single vector is an eigenvector, the coefficient vectors (including their signs under the re-orientation) for different choices of terminals must agree up to a common factor. This is exactly Proposition prop:added-1, which is stated without proof and is never explicitly invoked; unlike the analogous Proposition prw, the required argument must also track the case distinction in ψ and the orientation-dependent signs, so it is a nontrivial missing step.

failure_location.quote: Graph-tree-induced edge coefficients are invariant to the choice of terminals up to a common factor.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a proof of Proposition prop:added-1 (a re-rooting argument parallel to that of Proposition prw, handling the ψ case split and the orientation-induced signs) and invoke it explicitly in the proof of the Theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the main theorem (and hence the corollary on sharpness of the Hypothesis) is incomplete until the invariance of the (G,τ)-induced coefficients under change of terminals, including signs, is established.
issues.title: Main theorem's proof depends on unproved terminal-invariance of (G,τ)-induced coefficients
issues.why_classification: The result appears true (it checks on examples) and the fix is a contained lemma, but it requires a genuine new argument rather than a routine local edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we maximized the value of the \emph{target function} measuring the least deviation of the given subspace from all the same-dimensional coordinate subspaces
Since principle angles are arccosines of singular values of the corresponding submatrices.

issues.failure_explanation: The target function is defined as the least deviation (an angle) and is maximized by Algorithm 1, whose extremal value is arccos(1/sqrt(n)). Algorithm 2 instead tests the returned value d against 1/sqrt(n) ± ε and declares the Hypothesis refuted when d > 1/sqrt(n) + ε. If d is the angle, the thresholds are wrong (any angle above 1/sqrt(n) radians, including the extremal one, would falsely refute the Hypothesis). If d is instead the cosine max_I σ_min, then Algorithm 1 maximizes the wrong direction and refutation should be d < 1/sqrt(n) − ε. Under neither reading does the pseudocode deliver its stated output contract.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix the pseudocode consistently: either compare the angle d with arccos(1/sqrt(n)) ± ε, or define d as the cosine, minimize it in Algorithm 1, and reverse the refutation inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix pseudocode does not correctly compute the set of extremal subspaces as written; the numerical claims of Section 2 rest on the intended (unstated) consistent version. No formal result depends on it.
issues.title: Algorithm 2 compares the target function with 1/sqrt(n) inconsistently with its definition and optimization direction
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the comparison (once the meaning of d is fixed) restores the intended procedure; no theorem depends on the algorithm.
